extracted.subtask_description: Official KIPO procedural and substantive criteria for handling examination deferral/extension, document service, personal interviews, amendments (especially in response to final rejection), and decisions to grant or reject patents. Covers examiner duties, notification content, admissibility rules, and procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of examination deferral/extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination or extension of processing period shall be reported to the head of Examination Unit, and be notified to the concerned applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an examiner defers examination or extends processing, the fact must be reported up the chain and applicant notified. (Context: general duty to report and notify.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review of deferred/extended applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application whose examination or processing has been already deferred or extended respectively, an examiner shall review more than one time a month to confirm whether the reasons causing deferral or extension have been resolved or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If review confirms reasons cleared up, examiner shall conduct the examination by the termination date of the extension or deferral. Examiner must re-check frequently (at least monthly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on repeated extension/deferral when cause imputable to examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner considers the examination to be deferred and the processing period to be extended again because the application does not overcome the previous deferral or extension reason or new reasons occur, it shall be reported to the head of the examination division and the deferral or extension shall be made within two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, when extension is due to outsourcing prior art search, external consultation, consultation examination, or other reasons listed (grounds ④ and ⑥), the extension can be made again only in case of causes not imputable to the examiner. Reasons not imputable include late delivery of prior art search reports or delayed receipt of copies from external institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of reasons for further deferral/extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner once again decides to defer the examination or extend the processing period according to the abovementioned case, he/she notifies the applicant specific reasons of deferral or extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any repeated deferral/extension decisions must be accompanied by specific reasons communicated to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending patent trial/proceeding as ground for deferral
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent trial or proceeding related to the application concerned being pending is a ground for examination deferral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The case includes administrative trial or litigation on the concerned application procedure; pending proceedings justify deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of later‑filed applications on identical invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than two patent applications are filed on the identical invention, the examiner shall defer examination for later-filed applications until the prior-filed application has been processed or has been laid-open or registered. However, where the later-filed application can be rejected based on the same ground as the prior-filed application, the examiner can start examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed start-of-examination rules depend on: identicalness of applicants, disclosure status (laid-open/not laid-open). Table summarizes outcomes (e.g., if identical applicants & prior filed laid-open => examination conducted; if identical applicants & prior not laid-open => examination conducted with Article 36(1) rejection notified, patentability determined after confirming claims of prior-filed application; if different applicants and prior not laid-open => examination deferred until disclosure). Examiner must apply Article 36(1) when finalizing decision after prior-filed's claim scope determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination after prior-filed application processed
rubrics_metrics.description: When the prior-filed application is examined or laid open or registered after examination on later-filed applications is deferred, the examiner may conduct examination on later-filed application but shall make the final decision applying Article 36(1) once the scope of claim of the prior-filed application is determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may start examination but final patentability decision must account for prior-filed claim scope (Article 36(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document service: general method and receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents shall be served by registered mail except where the party or agent receives in person or uses information network. In case of sending by post mail, the registration receipt shall be kept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special service methods apply for trial rulings or written decisions per postal laws. Keep registration receipts as proof of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document service to legitimate receiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents shall be served to a legitimate receiver, referring to an agent if appointed, sub-agent or agent appointed midway except for special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple agents, serve the agent listed first in the written application unless special cases. For multiple general-power agents, prefer the one appointed for the relevant case. If receiver incompetent, serve legal representative. For multiple applicants, serve elected representative or first-named applicant. Change of service address must be reported without delay. If receiver unjustifiably rejects service, sending date may be regarded as receiving date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service to residential/business address
rubrics_metrics.description: Service shall be made to residential or business address of an entitled receiver unless reporting other address for service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change of service address must be reported promptly. Refer to Part 1 General Rules for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by public notification when address unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents cannot be served because the residential or business address of the addressee is unclear (including inability to verify using Resident Registration Use System), documents shall be served by public notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (①) on document returns, file facts in system and examiner verifies address by telephone and resend with Guide to Report on Information Change; (②) if address confirmed by Resident Registration Use System identical to telephone-confirmed address, serve by public notification; if not identical, resend to address from Resident Registration Use System; (③) if resent to RRUS address and returned again, serve by public notification with no further confirmation. For corporations (RRUS not usable), exert maximum efforts to confirm correct address and send once to legal address before public notification. Examiner may adopt different methods case-by-case if it ensures proper sending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of alternate service methods
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may adopt a different service method where through case by case review an examiner finds a new service method for sure sending to a legitimate receiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service should generally follow Rules on Office Management and Patent Net System but flexibility allowed for effective delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and grounds for personal interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may have a personal interview with the party where requested by the party or considered necessary for prompt and fair examination. Cases requiring personal interview include comparative explanation between claimed invention and prior art, clarification of ground for rejection, explanation of written argument, when subject matter is complicated, or other recognized needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews are ancillary methods to aid understanding and should be used when other communications (phone/email) insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting and granting personal interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Party requests interview by fax, telephone, information network (including e-mail), or written application in person. Each application requires an individual interview request, except if multiple applications are assigned to the same examiner the applicant may file one request for all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request can be filed after examination begins but not later than decision to grant; for applications decided to be rejected, party may request until an appeal trial is filed. Examiner may request/set a date only when telephone discussion is insufficient. Dates may change by agreement and must be logged. Examiner should respond actively but may ask to modify/disregard requests that are plain business contact, general questions, repetitive, or unrelated. Communications about interviews must include dates, persons, due date and form of interview, and contact number, recorded in the Patent Examination Processing System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal interview format and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal interview is face-to-face in principle; video phone interviews allowed using designated facilities. Examiner shall in advance review relevant documents and print them if necessary. If prior contact confirms discussion topic, examiner shall organize related issues in advance. Examiner may request party to provide reference documents or multimedia related to prior art in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation improves effectiveness; examiner may ask for materials. Use KIPO meeting/video facilities as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate interviewee and proxy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before an interview, examiner shall confirm whether a participant is a legitimate interviewee: applicant (or corporate representative), agent of the application, or a person with an evidential statement showing legitimate entrustee (sub-agent). A participant with delegation limited to personal interview must submit a proxy statement at every interview (may combine delegations for multiple interviews into one proxy stating all application numbers). A legitimate interviewee may be accompanied by an inventor or person related to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper authority to speak for application; require proxies where delegations are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview log contents and sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interview log, examiner shall state application number, name of examiner and participants, and contents and result of interview. The interview log, sealed with signatures of examiner and participants, shall be submitted to an officer in charge at the patent customer service center. Contents of the interview shall be included in the examination report of the Patent Examination Processing System. When opinions on restricted issues are exchanged, the opinion shall be briefly stated in the interview log by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep formal, signed records; include in exam record; summarize restricted exchanges succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct and limits of interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall proceed swiftly on the basis of personal interviews and any agreements made during an interview shall be conducted within the shortest time possible. A personal interview shall not be a basis for an examiner to simplify or omit requisite statements in the notification of the ground for rejection or written decision to reject. If a new ground for rejection is discovered after an interview, the examiner shall communicate the purport to the party by notice and continue examination. Examiner may request submission of materials presented at interview. Principle is one interview per application, but if necessary it can be held up to two times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews facilitate process but do not replace formal notice/decision requirements. Agreements are to be implemented quickly; request supporting materials when needed. If interview occurs during written-argument submission period, participants must submit promised documents per agreement; deviation must be communicated. Applicants cannot rely on interviews to omit required written argument statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal interview on visit procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request an examiner visit (personal interview on visit) online. Examiner contacts by telephone to determine need; visit allowed only if telephone communication difficult or necessary for prompt and accurate examination. Visits are in principle carried out at Regional Intellectual Property Centers but may occur elsewhere by mutual agreement. Changing dates and keeping interview log must comply with general personal interview procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visits are exceptional, require justification and follow same logging/authority rules as other interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for handling amendments responsive to final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike non-final rejection, when receiving amendment in response to notice of the final grounds for rejection, an examiner shall determine whether to refuse to enter the amendment before assessing patentability and confirm matters to be examined. If applicant argues that final rejection necessitated by amendment is inappropriate, examiner shall review appropriateness considering applicant's assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must decide whether final-rejection classification was correct and whether to admit amendment; decision processes differ from non-final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action when final rejection necessitated by amendment was inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where issuance of the final rejection necessitated by amendment is deemed inappropriate, an examiner shall not refuse to enter but admit the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final classification inappropriate, admit amendment and continue examination accordingly. If grounds indicated in final rejection are not overcome, examiner will take actions per specified cases, e.g., notify grounds again instead of rejecting if no amendment or limited amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling applicant treating final rejection as non-final
rubrics_metrics.description: Where final rejection necessitated by amendment is notified but applicant submits amendment treating it as non-final (arguing inappropriateness and responding accordingly), examiner shall make a decision to reject the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants cannot convert a final-rejection procedure into a non-final reply to avoid consequences; examiner must enforce final status resulting in decision to reject if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of admission/refusal for multiple amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant in response to the final notification submits multiple amendments within the period designated for written argument, an examiner shall determine whether he/she admit or refuse to enter the amendments in reverse order of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process amendments starting from the most recent submission backward to earlier ones to determine admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter amendments that create new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment in response to final rejection fails to meet the amendment scope prescribed in Article 47(2) and (3), or where new grounds for rejection occur from the amendment (excluding certain deletions), the amendment shall be refused to be entered. However, if a new ground can be cured by ex‑officio amendment, the examiner shall approve the amendment and carry out subsequent procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New grounds include deficiencies in description or new novelty/inventive-step issues caused by the amendment. Exclusions and ex‑officio amendment matters are referenced (Part IV, Chapter 2 and Part 2, Chapter 4). Several illustrative examples are provided in the text showing admissions and refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and exclusion of 'new ground for rejection' after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new ground for rejection' refers to when the submitted amendment causes unprecedented grounds for rejection (e.g., deficiency in description or new novelty/inventive step issues). It does not include grounds which have been noticed prior to the amendment or grounds which had existed without notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate when an amendment (e.g., adding element C) introduces a need to cite additional prior art, constituting a new ground and possibly justifying refusal to enter amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of claim deletions that generate new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment was deletion of claims and subsequently generated a new ground for rejection (e.g., dependent claim now deficient), an examiner shall not refuse to enter the amendment for that reason alone. An examiner shall admit the amendment unless there are other reasons for refusal, and then notify the new rejection grounds in the final rejection necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletion that causes deficiencies may be treated as admitted; if deletion results in clerical error (remaining claims understandable excluding deleted claim), treat as clerical error and subject to ex‑officio amendment rather than refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written decision for refusal to enter amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to refuse to enter amendment shall be made in writing separately from the decision to reject an application, specifying reasons why amendment had to be refused to be entered for the subsequent procedural convenience for an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants cannot appeal refusal to enter amendment during substantive examination; such issues are dealt with in trial against the decision to reject. Refusals made before revocation in ex‑officio reexamination or before request for reexamination also cannot be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination after admission of amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment is appropriately made, an examiner shall admit the amendment and determine the specification to be examined after reflecting the amendment, followed by assessment of patentability, notifications and decision to grant or reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grounds for rejection are not overcome by the amendment, make decision to reject; otherwise grant patent. If other grounds are generated, notify applicant of newly found grounds (refer to Types of Notice). Examiner cannot later retroactively refuse to enter a previously admitted amendment if they overlooked its inappropriateness and proceeded to grant or notify rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination after refusal to enter amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: After refusing to enter amendment, examiner shall continue examining the pre-amended specification. Where reviewing the final rejection necessitated by amendment and discovering the ground not overcome, examiner shall make a decision to reject. Where examiner regards final rejection as inappropriate and discovers no other grounds, grant patent. If final rejection inappropriate but other grounds exist, notify those grounds again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue with original specification if amendment refused; follow appropriate notification or grant/reject sequence based on review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely decision to grant or reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Once completing the examination, an examiner shall make a decision to grant or reject without delay. Where examination of formalities discovers deficiency in application procedure, the final decision shall be made after the procedural deficiency is remedied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be prompt; procedural defects may delay final decision until remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of written decision to grant a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no ground for rejection is discovered, an examiner shall make a decision to grant a patent in writing with rationale attached. The written decision shall include application number, title of invention, name and address of applicant and agent, the text of decision of patentability and its rationale, number of claims to be patented, date of decision, matters amended ex officio, and examiner's sign and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner delivers a certified copy to applicant; decision is confirmed upon delivery. Special internal-consultation requirements apply for certain applications (e.g., filed by KIPO examiners or within 2 years of retirement or by supervised searchers) where examiner must consult with 3 persons including director/head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and contents of written decision to reject an application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant fails to overcome grounds for rejection, examiner shall make a decision to reject in writing with rationale attached. The written decision shall include application number, title of invention, name and address of applicant and agent, date of notice of grounds for rejection, text of decision and its rationale, date of decision to reject, and examiner's sign and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner delivers certified copy; decision confirmed when cannot be revoked (e.g., no appeal, trial decision supporting rejection). Examiner shall indicate determination on applicant's amendment where notified grounds were still not overcome and list issuable items in the written argument. If any claim contains grounds for rejection in multi-claim application, reject the application. Examiner shall not base rejection on unreasonable rationale other than already-notified grounds; to rely on new prior art examiner must notify that fact as a ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling third‑party information and unentitled filers before final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining an application with information provided by a third party as grounds for rejection or an application filed by an unentitled person, an examiner shall take requisite measures before making the final decision. For third‑party information, examiner shall notify the information provider of his/her decision and whether the provided information is used when the examination closes, except where the provider lacked capacity or the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure procedural fairness and notify contributors about usage of their submissions when examination concludes.
